questions.question: What is the average of all three-digit numbers divisible by 23?
questions.questionHtml: What is the average of all three-digit numbers divisible by 23?
questions.solution:
⇒ Smallest three-digit multiple of 23: 23 × 5 = 115

⇒ Largest three-digit multiple of 23: 23 × 43 = 989

⇒ Average = (115 + 989) ÷ 2 = 552

questions.question: A stationery shop ordered 6 dozen red pens and some additional dozen blue pens. The price of the red pens per dozen was three times that of the blue ones. Find the ratio of the number of dozens of red pens to the number of dozens of blue pens in the original order.

When the order was delivered, it was found that the number of dozens of the two colours had been interchanged. This increased the bill by 40%. questions.question: A flower vendor bought 200 flowers for ₹800. 20 flowers withered and became unsellable. At what price per flower should he sell the remaining flowers to earn a profit of 30% on his total cost?
questions.questionHtml: A flower vendor bought 200 flowers for ₹800. 20 flowers withered and became unsellable. At what price per flower should he sell the remaining flowers to earn a profit of 30% on his total cost?
questions.solution:
Sellable flowers ⇒ 200 − 20 = 180

Total selling price ⇒ 800 × (1 + 30 ÷ 100) = 800 × 1.3 = 1040

Price per flower ⇒ 1040 ÷ 180 = 5.78

questions.question: A solution consists acid and water in the ratio 5:3. If 4 litres of water is added, the new ratio becomes 5:4. What is the original quantity of acid in the solution?
questions.questionHtml: A solution consists acid and water in the ratio 5:3. If 4 litres of water is added, the new ratio becomes 5:4. What is the original quantity of acid in the solution?
questions.solution:
Let the original quantity of acid = 5x and water = 3x.

New water quantity = 3x + 4; New ratio: 5 ÷ 4.

(5x) ÷ (3x + 4) = 5 ÷ 4 ⇒ 5x × 4 = 5 × (3x + 4) ⇒ 20x = 15x + 20 ⇒ 5x = 20 ⇒ x = 4.

Original quantity of acid = 5x = 5 × 4 = 20 litres.

questions.question: A alone can complete a job in 12 days and B alone in 18 days. A and B agree to do the work for ₹ 7,200. With C's help they finish it in 5 days. How much should C be paid?
questions.questionHtml: A alone can complete a job in 12 days and B alone in 18 days. A and B agree to do the work for ₹ 7,200. With C's help they finish it in 5 days. How much should C be paid?
questions.solution:
⇒ LCM of 12 and 18 = 36 units; Efficiency of A = 36 ÷ 12 = 3 units/day; Efficiency of B = 36 ÷ 18 = 2 units/day.

⇒ Total work = 36 units; Combined efficiency of A + B + C = 36 ÷ 5 = 7.2 units/day.

⇒ Efficiency of C = 7.2 − 5 = 2.2 units/day; Ratio of work done = 3 : 2 : 2.2 = 30 : 20 : 22.

⇒ C's share = (22 ÷ 72) × 7200 = 2200.

  <text x="30" y="170" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#222222">⇒ Final B − Final A = (8x − 16) − (7x − 14 + 15) = 25</text>
  <text x="30" y="195" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#222222">⇒ x − 17 = 25 ⇒ x = 42</text>
  <text x="30" y="220" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#222222">⇒ Initial Mix = 20x = 20 × 42 = 840</text>
  
  <text x="30" y="255" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" font-weight="700" fill="#000000">∴ Answer = 840 litres</text>
</svg>

questions.question: The ratio of the time taken by A and B to complete a task is 3 : 2. If B can complete the task alone in 18 hours, how many hours will they take to complete the task if they work together?
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of the time taken by A and B to complete a task is 3 : 2. If B can complete the task alone in 18 hours, how many hours will they take to complete the task if they work together?
questions.solution:
Let time taken by A = 3x, time taken by B = 2x

⇒ 2x = 18 ⇒ x = 9 ⇒ Time taken by A = 27 hours

⇒ LCM of 27 and 18 = 54 units

⇒ Efficiency of A = 54 ÷ 27 = 2 units/hour, Efficiency of B = 54 ÷ 18 = 3 units/hour

⇒ Combined efficiency = 2 + 3 = 5 units/hour

⇒ Time taken together = 54 ÷ 5 = 10.8 hours

They all start from the same point at 9:00 a.m. and travel in the same direction with speeds of 10 km/h, 12 km/h, and 15 km/h respectively. How many times will all three of them meet at the starting point if they continue cycling until 1:00 p.m.?

They all start from the same point at 9:00 a.m. and travel in the same direction with speeds of 10 km/h, 12 km/h, and 15 km/h respectively.   </defs>

  <!-- ZONE 1: Circular Track Mechanism -->
  <circle cx="120" cy="85" r="65" stroke="#2255cc" stroke-width="2" fill="none" stroke-dasharray="5,3" />
  <path d="M 120,20 L 120,35" stroke="#555555" stroke-width="3" />

  <!-- Speed Indicators -->
  <path d="M 140,25 A 75,75 0 0 1 190,65" fill="none" stroke="#cc5500" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#arrO)" />

  <path d="M 155,35 A 85,85 0 0 1 205,95" fill="none" stroke="#6a1b9a" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#arrP)" />
  <text x="210" y="105" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#6a1b9a">12 km/h</text>

  <path d="M 170,45 A 95,95 0 0 1 215,130" fill="none" stroke="#007700" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#arrG)" />
  <text x="190" y="145" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#007700">15 km/h</text>

  <line x1="280" y1="120" x2="480" y2="120" stroke="#555555" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#arr)" />

  <text x="265" y="140" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#555555">9am</text>
  <text x="465" y="140" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#555555">1pm</text>

  <text x="440" y="100" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#cc0000">Meet 2</text>
  
  <text x="310" y="60" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#2255cc">Track = 2 km</text>
  <text x="310" y="80" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#222222">Duration = 4 hrs</text>

  <text x="30" y="195" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#222222">⇒ Lap Times: 2÷10, 2÷12, 2÷15 hr → 1/5, 1/6, 2/15 hr</text>
  <text x="30" y="220" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#222222">⇒ Meeting Interval = LCM(1/5, 1/6, 2/15) = 2 hours</text>

questions.question: A circular path of 3 m width runs around a circular park with radius 8 m. What is the area of the path?
questions.questionHtml: A circular path of 3 m width runs around a circular park with radius 8 m. What is the area of the path?
questions.solution:
Outer radius = 8 + 3 = 11 m

Area of outer circle = 3.14 × 112 = 3.14 × 121 = 379.94 m2

Area of inner circle = 3.14 × 82 = 3.14 × 64 = 200.96 m2

Area of path = 379.94 − 200.96 = 178.98 m2 ≈ 179 m2

questions.question: A sector of a circle having a radius of 10 cm and has a central angle of \( \frac{\pi}{6}\) radians. What is the area of the sector?
questions.questionHtml: A sector of a circle having a radius of 10 cm and has a central angle of \( \frac{\pi}{6}\) radians. What is the area of the sector?
questions.solution:
Area of sector = (1 ÷ 2) × r2 × θ

⇒ Area of sector = (1 ÷ 2) × 102 × (π ÷ 6)

⇒ Area of sector = 50 × (π ÷ 6) = 25π ÷ 3

⇒ Area of sector = (25 × 3.14) ÷ 3 = 26.17 cm2

questions.question: If sin A + cos A = √2 sin A, then what is the value of tanA?
questions.questionHtml: If sin A + cos A = √2 sin A, then what is the value of tanA?
questions.solution:
sinA + cosA = √2 sinA

⇒ cosA = sinA(√2 − 1)

⇒ tanA = sinA ÷ cosA = 1 ÷ (√2 − 1)

⇒ tanA = (√2 + 1) ÷ (2 − 1) = √2 + 1
